title: ABA/474/2024 of JIGNESH ALIAS MANISH SHAH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Anticipatory Bail Application No.474 of 2024
Jignesh @ Manish Shah ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, Advocates for the applicant.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant seeks anticipatory bail in FIR No.3 of
2024, under Section 420 IPC and Section 66D of the
Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police
Station Kotwali Pauri, District Pauri Garhwal.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, the informants were
working in their resort business in Pauri Garhwal. They
came with the co-accused, who stayed in their resort,
thereafter, the co-accused introduced the applicant to the
informants. The applicant introduced himself that he
runs a Maha Kali Group Company which is a trading
company and induced the informants to invest their
money. The investment was made. The FIR is quite in
detail. The informants have also taken gold loan for
investment. It also records that the applicant came so
close to the informants that he also started operating the

2
bank account, user password, etc. of the informants.
Subsequently, the informants realised that they have
been cheated.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that no money was transferred in the account of
the applicant. It is argued that it is highly improbable
that some persons would give the bank's password and
user ID to some other persons to operate it.
5. Learned State Counsel would also submit that
the applicant has also involved in similar nature of cases.
He induced the informants to invest money assuring high
returns.
6. It is the stage of anticipatory bail. Much of the
discussion at this stage is not expected of. To the extent
of appreciating the controversy, the matter may be
examined with the caveat that any observation, made at
this stage, shall have no bearing at any subsequent stage
of the case.
7. As per the prosecution, the informants were
induced by the applicant to invest money in the trading
company.

3
8. Having considered the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that this is a case fit for anticipatory
bail.
9. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
10. In the eventuality of arrest, the applicant shall
be enlarged on anticipatory bail subject to his furnishing
a personal bond with two sureties, each in the like
amount, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer ("AO").
In addition to it, the applicant shall also comply with the
following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall co-operate with the
investigation.
(ii) The applicant shall not approach any witness,
whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall not leave the country
without prior permission of the concerned
court.
(iv) The applicant shall deposit their passport with
the AO. The passport may only be returned by
the order of the court concerned. In case the
applicant does not have passport, he shall give
an undertaking to that effect to the AO.
(v) The applicant shall also give an undertaking on
(i), (ii) & (iii) above.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J)
 09.07.2024
Ravi
